battle.name: 阿薩爾哈東對埃及的戰爭
battle.theater: 尼羅河三角洲與孟斐斯
battle.brief: 公元前671年，亞述王阿薩爾哈東自哈蘭沿幼發拉底河西行、沿海入埃及，於尼羅河三角洲擊敗法老塔哈卡，攻陷孟斐斯，把下埃及收為行省。卡面這件斯巴達長矛並非兩國正統武裝，而是兩軍中希臘傭兵所持的重步兵長槍，在埃及防線的盾牆中與亞述的密集弓陣相持。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 這場戰爭是公元前七世紀前半亞述帝國對埃及第二十五王朝的戰役，交戰地帶在尼羅河三角洲與孟斐斯，正式爆發於公元前671年，捲入其後669年至663年一連串亞述王征埃及的行動。亞述一方是阿卡德語稱埃薩哈東的亞述王阿薩爾哈東，他於公元前680年即位，執政已逾十年；他的軍隊由王家居中的常備重步兵、弓手、雙輪輕車、騎兵、工兵與攻城工匠組成，各省總督與團隊首領另率分遣隊伍，命令靠騎使與信鴿傳遞，作戰意圖與行軍序列多由御前書記與占卜檔案定下。埃及一方是第二十五王朝，即努比亞的庫施王族建立的王朝，國王塔哈卡在位於公元前690年至675年；他以三角洲為根據，軍隊由埃及本地徵召的步兵與弓手、庫舒來的努比亞重步兵與弓手，以及受僱的伊奧尼亞與卡里亞希臘傭兵組成，另有王室近衛與巡邊的游騎兵。地緣上，亞述要跨過幼發拉底與地中海，埃及則據尼羅河三角洲與孟斐斯這座舊都；若要支援西頓、推羅等受亞述壓迫的城邦，埃及的援助必須自三角洲越過沙漠與西奈山才能送達。
countriesEn: This war was a campaign of the Assyrian empire against Egypt's Twenty-fifth Dynasty in the first half of the seventh century BC. The ground of the fighting was the Nile delta and the city of Memphis; the campaign opened in 671 BC and drew in the chain of Assyrian expeditions to Egypt that ran from 669 down to 663. On the Assyrian side stood the empire of Esarhaddon, the Assyrian king called Aššar-iddin in Akkadian, who had taken the throne in 680 BC and had ruled for more than a decade. His army combined a standing household body of heavy infantry, archers, light two-wheeled cars, cavalry, sappers and siege craftsmen; provincial governors and company commanders led detached columns of their own, orders travelled by mounted messenger and pigeon post, and the plan of operations and the order of march were settled in the royal secretariat and in the omen archives. On the Egyptian side stood the Twenty-fifth Dynasty, the Nubian Kushite house that had reunited Egypt, with the pharaoh Taharqa, who reigned from 690 to 675 BC. He held the delta, and his forces were made up of Egyptian levies of foot and archers, Nubian heavy infantry and archers sent up from Kush, and hired Ionian and Carian Greek mercenaries, together with the royal guard and the border-riding cavalry. Geographically, Assyria had to cross the Euphrates and the sea, while Egypt sat on the delta and on Memphis, the old capital; and to aid Sidon, Tyre and the other Phoenician cities under Assyrian pressure, Egyptian help had to travel out of the delta across the desert and over the slopes of Sinai.
people: 阿薩爾哈東是亞述巴尼拔的長子，父王指定他繼承王位，他於公元前680年登基；他的御前會議記錄與致占卜師的書信保存至今，其中一封問卜書信提到出征埃及的籌劃，是確定這場戰爭時間表的重要材料。他沒有用「隱王」那套安排把王位交給他人，反而把兄弟沙馬什-舒姆-烏金與太子亞述巴尼拔留在都城與前線交替任事，自己帶著主力遠征。埃及方面的核心是法老塔哈卡，這位庫施出身的君主把埃及重新統一在第二十五王朝之下，重整軍制、削弱阿蒙神廟的權力，並把手伸到西頓與推羅；他在孟斐斯失守後退回庫舒的都城納帕塔。據亞述方面的記錄，埃及的祭司曾向亞述求援，控訴對神廟財產的徵用，這類說法出自交戰一方，須有所保留。公元前672年亞述在埃及另立奈科一世為附庸王，他於669年再度反叛身亡；其子普薩姆提克一世後來於663年前後即位，是第廿六王朝的開國者，埃及重獲獨立的關鍵人物就是他。希臘傭兵的指揮權操在埃及方面的希臘將領手中，其姓名在不同抄本中寫法不一，本文只作一名希臘將領處理，不強行拼合人名。
peopleEn: Esarhaddon was the eldest son of Ashurbanipal, whom his father nominated as his successor, and he ascended the throne in 680 BC. The minutes of his council and the letters he sent to his diviners survive, and one of those letters of inquiry mentions the planning of the expedition to Egypt, which is an important document for the dating of this war. He did not use the arrangement of the hidden king to hand the throne to another, but left his brother Shamash-shum-ukin and his own son Ashurbanipal to hold court and the front in turn while he marched with the main body. The pivot of the Egyptian side was the pharaoh Taharqa, a Kushite ruler who had brought Egypt back together under the Twenty-fifth Dynasty, reorganised the army, cut down the power and the property of the temple of Amun, and reached as far as Sidon and Tyre; after Memphis fell he withdrew to Napata, the capital of Kush. The Assyrian account says that Egyptian clerics appealed to Assyria and denounced the seizure of temple property, but such a claim is made by one of the belligerents and has to be held with reserve. In 672 BC Assyria set up Necho I in Egypt as a client king; he rebelled again in 669 and died, and his son Psamtik I, founder of the Twenty-sixth Dynasty, took the throne around 663 BC and became the man who restored Egyptian independence. The Greek mercenaries were commanded by a Greek officer in Egyptian pay; his name is written differently in different copies, so he is handled here only as a Greek commander and no attempt is made to force a single name.
kits: 卡面這件斯巴達長矛是典型的hoplite重步兵長槍，槍身約兩米，櫸木桿，前端嵌青銅矛頭，尾端有青銅套以便插地支撐；它配的不是短劍，而是直徑近一米的aspis圓盾，加上青銅頭盔、胸甲與脛甲，靠密集方陣的盾牆和兩米長的刺擊距離作戰。要說清它在這場戰爭裡的位置，必須先講明一點：它不是亞述或埃及任何一國的正統武裝，卻確實出現在這兩個營壘裡。亞述人稱希臘人為「雅瓦納」，稱卡里亞人為「卡爾基亞」；尼尼微王宮那組「埃薩哈東營」浮雕裡，就有身持圓盾與長槍的希臘雇兵站在亞述軍營之中，這是亞述軍中確有希臘重步兵的最直接圖像證據。而埃及方面自第二十五王朝起也長期僱用伊奧尼亞與卡里亞傭兵，671年守孟斐斯的防線上就有他們的身影。除長槍外，亞述軍的裝備還包括鐵矛、銅刃短劍、骨柄投石索、複合弓、鱗甲與札甲、柳條盾，以及攻城用的木製撞槌、壘土斜坡，與隨軍的鐵匠、木匠；埃及與庫舒一方則有銅矛、斧、弓、獸皮盾、努比亞的長弓、雙輪載具與巨獸。糧秣方面，遠征船隊從腓尼基地區運糧，沿途靠劫掠與埃及城鎮繳納的穀物、銀金維持。
kitsEn: The card shows a typical hoplite dory: a shaft about two metres long, made of ash, with a bronze head fitted at the front and a bronze butt-spike at the rear that could be planted in the ground to steady the thrust. It was used not with a short sword but with an aspis, a round shield nearly a metre across, together with a bronze helmet, a corselet and greaves, and it fought inside a dense phalanx whose shield wall and two-metre reach settled the business. To place it in this war one point must be made first: the dory was the standard arm of neither Assyria nor Egypt, and yet it did appear in both camps. The Assyrians called the Greeks Yauna and the Carians Karkiya, and the reliefs of the Camp of Esarhaddon from the palace at Nineveh show Greek mercenaries with round shields and long spears standing inside an Assyrian camp, which is the most direct visual evidence that Greek heavy infantry served in the Assyrian army. Egypt, from the Twenty-fifth Dynasty onward, likewise employed Ionian and Carian mercenaries for long stretches, and they stood in the line that held Memphis in 671. Besides the long spear the Assyrian equipment list included iron-tipped spears, short bronze-edged swords, bone-handled slings, composite bows, scale and lamellar armour, wicker shields, and, for siege work, wooden battering rams, earthen causeways, and the smiths and carpenters who marched with the column. The Egyptian and Kushite side had bronze-tipped spears, axes, bows, hide-covered shields, the long Nubian bow, two-wheeled vehicles and beasts of burden. For supply, the expedition carried grain by sea from the Phoenician coast and lived off plunder and off the grain, silver and gold taken from the Egyptian towns.
tactics: 亞述的戰役方案是先海後陸的縱深推進：主力自哈蘭沿幼發拉底河西行至腓尼基海岸，在推羅與以色列一線征糧，再由腓尼基船隊載兵越海，在尼羅河三角洲東端的佩魯西翁一帶登陸；登陸後兵分兩路，一路封住三角洲通往沙漠的出口，另一路沿尼羅河西岸南下直取孟斐斯，把埃及王軍堵在城牆與河道之間，再以壘土、攻城塔與撞槌圍城，斷其水陸補給，同時把孟斐斯變成亞述在埃及的落腳點。埃及的應對是先以步兵列陣於城北的開闊地，弓手在後列成數道縱深，雙輪載具與騎兵在兩翼護住陣腳；希臘傭兵被放在防線最前，以方盾結成的密集盾牆頂住亞述密集的箭雨與短兵接觸，長槍從盾縫間刺出，等亞述步兵逼近到兩三步之內才發動齊刺。塔哈卡放棄孟斐斯後，隊伍沿尼羅河谷南撤，往納帕塔方向行軍，步兵與弓手交替掩護，渡口與井驛被破壞以拖延追兵。亞述遠征的補給線極長，除船運外也靠沿途城鎮繳納與徵用，最後是靠劫掠孟斐斯的財富維持再遠征。
tacticsEn: The Assyrian plan was to advance first by sea and then by land. The main body travelled west from Harran along the Euphrates to the Phoenician coast, took tribute in the district of Tyre and Israel, and was then carried across the water by Phoenician transports to land near Pelusium at the eastern mouth of the delta. After the landing the column divided: one part closed the exits from the delta into the desert, the other marched south along the west bank of the Nile straight at Memphis, shutting the Egyptian royal army between the city walls and the river channels, and then surrounded the place with earthen ramparts, siege towers and rams, cutting its supply by water and by land, while turning Memphis into the Assyrian foothold in Egypt. Egypt's answer was to array the infantry in the open ground north of the city, with the archers behind them in several ranks of depth and the two-wheeled cars and the cavalry covering the wings; the Greek mercenaries were placed at the head of the line, their tightly packed shield wall taking the Assyrian arrow fall and the shock of close combat, the long spears striking out through the gaps of the shields and engaging only when the Assyrian infantry had closed to two or three paces. When Taharqa gave up Memphis, his column withdrew south up the Nile valley towards Napata, foot and archers taking turns to cover one another, and the fords and wells on the line were broken up to hold off the pursuit. The Assyrian line of supply was extremely long; besides the sea transport it ran on requisitions from the towns along the way, and the last stage was paid for out of the plunder of Memphis.
data: 可以核對的數字不多，這場戰爭的細節多靠亞述王室的敘事銘文與巴比倫的年代記殘篇支撐，亞述人慣用的夸張與精確數字並存。時間線上：埃薩哈東公元前680年即位，671年出兵，672年在埃及另立奈科一世，669年再征埃及並在回程中病逝於尼尼微；他的兒子亞述巴尼拔667年在三角洲再敗埃及與庫舒的聯軍，663年攻入底比斯劫掠，亞述在埃及的統治至此終結，663至664年間普薩姆提克一世即位。地理上：哈蘭到孟斐斯的陸海全程約一千五百公里以上；尼羅河三角洲東西寬約二百公里；佩魯西翁到孟斐斯沿河道約一百五十公里；孟斐斯在尼羅河西岸、今開羅以南約二十公里。兵力方面，亞述的分遣隊來自多省，銘文只留下若干團隊的名錄，總數無可靠記載，只能說是以萬計的混合部隊；埃及方能確定的，是庫舒來的努比亞重步兵與弓手為其主力，數目同樣只到以萬計的程度。傷亡數字沒有留下可信記載；能算得出的損失是城池與政權：孟斐斯陷落，國王出逃。
dataEn: Few figures can be checked. The detail of this war rests on the narrative inscriptions of the Assyrian king and on fragments of Babylonian chronographic texts, and the Assyrian habit of magnification sits side by side with their exact numbers. On the chronology: Esarhaddon took the throne in 680 BC, marched in 671, set up Necho I in Egypt in 672, campaigned into Egypt again in 669 and died at Nineveh on the way home; his son Ashurbanipal beat the Egyptian and Kushite allies in the delta in 667 and carried fire into Thebes in 663, which ended Assyrian rule in Egypt, and Psamtik I took the throne between 663 and 664. On geography: the road and sea route from Harran to Memphis ran to something over fifteen hundred kilometres; the Nile delta is about two hundred kilometres wide from east to west; it is about a hundred and fifty kilometres from Pelusium to Memphis along the river; and Memphis stood on the west bank of the Nile, some twenty kilometres south of the site of modern Cairo. On the numbers of men: the Assyrian detachments were drawn from many provinces, the inscriptions preserve only the names of certain units, and there is no dependable total, so it can be said only that the column was a mixed force numbering in the tens of thousands; on the Egyptian side the certain fact is that Nubian heavy infantry and archers from Kush formed the core, and their numbers again reach only the order of tens of thousands. No reliable figures for killed or wounded survive. What can be counted as loss is city and kingship: Memphis fell and the king went out into exile.
cause: 要理解這場戰爭為何打成，先要看塔哈卡在埃及做的事。第二十五王朝的庫施王族把埃及重新收束在一個王朝之下，塔哈卡一面整軍，一面削弱阿蒙神廟的權力與財產，這在神廟與祭司集團眼中是背叛；亞述方面的記錄說埃及的祭司曾向亞述求援，這種說法出自交戰一方，只能視為一方的說辭。真正的戰略原因更直接：塔哈卡支持西頓與推羅抵抗亞述，亞述於公元前677年攻破西頓，公元前675年又取走阿什凱倫，沿海各城被迫改朝；只要埃及繼續從三角洲向這些城市輸送兵力與金銀，亞述在黎凡特的整頓就做不完成。加上塞浦路斯與推羅的商運利權、腓尼基的航運線一併捲入其中，亞述必須把埃及的軍力收編到自己的秩序裡，否則後方永遠不安定。於是公元前671年，阿薩爾哈東把西線戰事收束成一場直搗尼羅河的遠征，目標是塔哈卡本人，以及三角洲的兵源、稅源與港口。
causeEn: To understand why this war was fought, one has to begin with what Taharqa did in Egypt. The Kushite house of the Twenty-fifth Dynasty had drawn Egypt back under a single dynasty; Taharqa reorganised the army while cutting down the wealth and the authority of the temple of Amun, which the priesthood read as betrayal, and the Assyrian record says that Egyptian clerics appealed to Assyria, a claim made by one of the belligerents and only to be taken as one party's account. The strategic reason is more direct. Taharqa backed Sidon and Tyre against Assyria; Assyria broke Sidon in 677 BC and took Ashkelon in 675, and the coastal cities were compelled to change sides. As long as Egypt kept feeding men and gold out of the delta to those cities, the work of reordering the Levant could never be finished by Assyria. With the commerce of Cyprus and Tyre and the shipping of Phoenicia pulled into the same tangle, Assyria had to fold Egypt's military into its own order, or its rear would remain unsettled for good. So in 671 BC Esarhaddon compressed the western war into a single thrust at the Nile, aimed at Taharqa himself and at the manpower, the taxes and the harbours of the delta.
impact: 這場戰爭的第一重後果，是埃及的地理與政治版圖被改寫。公元前671年之後，下埃及被編入亞述帝國的南方行省，以孟斐斯為行政中心，直到亞述巴尼拔在663年劫掠底比斯，行省才告崩解；663至664年間普薩姆提克一世重建第廿六王朝，埃及恢復了自己的王朝，也恢復了自己的對外政策。第二重後果在軍事制度上：埃及在此役中嘗到希臘傭兵的力量，也嘗到其極限，於是第廿六王朝把僱傭兵制度長期化、海軍化，希臘人從邊緣的雇兵變成埃及軍隊的骨架，這條線一直延伸到後來埃及直面波斯與馬其頓。第三重後果在東地中海：亞述打通了到尼羅河的補給與航道，把埃蘭殘部、腓尼基與埃及串成一條可控的南方走廊，卻也把亞述拖進一場遠離底格里斯河核心的消耗戰。還有一層人事上的後果，被俘的埃及工匠、金屬匠與書吏被帶回亞述及其屬地，這種技藝與人力的轉移，是亞述晚期工藝與行政仍能維持的原因之一。
impactEn: The first consequence of this war was a redrawing of the map of Egypt. After 671 BC the lower Nile was organised as a southern province of the Assyrian empire with Memphis as its administrative centre, and that province held together until Ashurbanipal looted Thebes in 663; between 663 and 664 Psamtik I rebuilt the Twenty-sixth Dynasty, and Egypt regained both a dynasty of its own and a foreign policy of its own. The second consequence was institutional and military: having measured the strength of Greek mercenaries in this campaign and also their limits, the Twenty-sixth Dynasty made mercenary service a standing system and put it to sea, and the Greek went from being an edge mercenary to being the frame of the Egyptian army, a line running straight on to the later confrontation of Egypt with Persia and with Macedon. The third consequence lay in the eastern Mediterranean. Assyria had opened a supply line and a sea lane to the Nile, stringing the remnants of Elam, Phoenicia and Egypt into a controllable southern corridor; but it had also dragged itself into a war of attrition far from the core of the Euphrates. There was a human consequence as well: captured Egyptian craftsmen, metalworkers and scribes were taken back to Assyria and its provinces, and that transfer of skill and of hands is one of the reasons the late Assyrian machine of industry and administration could still be kept running.
result: 公元前671年的戰果由亞述掌握：法老塔哈卡在三角洲之戰中被逐，退回庫舒的都城納帕塔，孟斐斯淪陷，下埃及被收為亞述行省，埃薩哈東於672年在孟斐斯立奈科一世為附庸王。奈科一世在669年反叛，埃及再度兵變，埃薩哈東再度出兵，重新控制孟斐斯並把它設為亞述在埃及的首都；他卻在回程途中病逝於尼尼微，即公元前669年，王位由亞述巴尼拔接手。亞述巴尼拔於667年在三角洲擊敗坦塔曼尼的軍隊，663年攻入底比斯劫掠，亞述在埃及的統治至此終結；普薩姆提克一世隨後在三角洲站穩，驅走殘餘的亞述勢力與庫舒干預。第廿六王朝由此開啟，埃及再度以穀物、銀金與地中海航運支援黎凡特諸城，與亞述、然後巴比倫的西進正面相撞；下一場大戰便是公元前626年埃及與新巴比倫在卡爾西米什的交鋒，而那場戰爭裡的埃及軍隊，仍然大量僱用希臘長槍重步兵。
resultEn: The outcome of 671 BC was Assyria's: the pharaoh Taharqa was driven out of the delta after the fighting there and withdrew to Napata, the Kushite capital; Memphis fell; the lower Nile was taken as an Assyrian province; and in 672 BC Esarhaddon set up Necho I in Memphis as a client king. Necho rebelled in 669 and Egypt rose again, so Esarhaddon marched out a second time, retook Memphis and made it the capital of Assyrian Egypt; but he died at Nineveh on the return journey in 669 BC, and his son Ashurbanipal succeeded him. Ashurbanipal defeated the army of Tantamani in the delta in 667 and carried fire into Thebes in 663, which ended Assyrian rule in Egypt; Psamtik I then held the delta, drove out the remaining Assyrian presence and the Kushite intervention, and the Twenty-sixth Dynasty began. Egypt once more supported the cities of the Levant with grain, silver and gold and with the carrying trade of the Mediterranean, and came into direct collision with Assyria and then with Babylonia; the next great war was the clash of Egypt and Neo-Babylon at Carchemish in 626 BC, and the Egyptian army in that battle still employed large numbers of Greek long-spear heavy infantry.
